access_notes: Create an app in the Discord Developer Portal to self-serve client ID/secret and optional bot token; production scale and privileged intents require passing Discord’s app review/verification.
mcp_notes: Community MCP servers exist; there is no official MCP server from Discord.
blocker_notes: App Verification is required to scale beyond 100 servers; Privileged Intents require review once the app reaches ≥10,000 users, with annual re-review.

evidence.quote: “OAuth2 enables application developers to build applications… We support the authorization code grant, the implicit grant, client credentials, and some modified special‑for‑Discord flows for Bots and Webhooks.”
“Bot users are… authenticated using the bot token found in your app’s settings. Unlike the normal OAuth2 flow, bot users have full access to most API routes…”
“Verification is required for your app to scale past 100 servers.”
“The review threshold is now based on user count… If your app has fewer than 10,000 users, you can continue… Once your app reaches 10,000 users, you’ll need to apply… Apps must now reapply annually…”
“This repository contains the public preview of the OpenAPI 3.1 specification for Discord’s API… ‘openapi.json’ is the standard spec…”
“Discord supports two distinct types of webhooks… incoming webhooks… and webhook events for receiving notifications from Discord when something happens in your app.”

_trail.quote: "Verification is required for your app to scale past 100 servers."
